headline_marked: Woman testifies: [[Daughter raped by AL leaders]] after she gave statement on husband's death
headline: Woman testifies: Daughter raped by AL leaders after she gave statement on husband's death
summary: Ruma Begum testified at the International Crimes Tribunal that her daughter committed suicide after being raped by Awami League leaders as retaliation for her testimony.
details: Ruma Begum testified before the International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Monday, alleging that her eldest daughter, Lamia, was raped by Awami League leaders after Ruma had provided a statement to investigators regarding the death of her husband, Md. Jasim Uddin.

Jasim Uddin was shot and killed during the July 2024 protests. Ruma testified that her husband was shot in the chest and fingers by police and Chhatra League members in front of the Allah Karim Mosque in Mohammadpur, Dhaka.
According to the witness, her daughter Lamia became mentally devastated after the rape occurred and subsequently committed suicide.
The testimony was given in a case against 28 people, including former DSCC Mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Tapos and AL Presidium member Jahangir Kabir Nanak, for crimes against humanity.

Ruma described the harrowing experience of trying to recover her husband's body from hospitals and police stations, claiming she was told by a police officer that clearance was denied due to 'orders from above'.
She further alleged that the police in Dumki, Patuakhali, ordered her to quickly bury the husband's body immediately upon arrival at their village home.
caption:
A mother's testimony at the International Crimes Tribunal reveals a harrowing tale of retaliation: her daughter was raped and later committed suicide.

Ruma Begum testified before the International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Monday, alleging that her eldest daughter, Lamia, was raped by Awami League leaders after Ruma had provided a statement to investigators regarding the death of her husband, Md. Jasim Uddin.

Jasim Uddin was shot and killed during the July 2024 protests. Ruma testified that her husband was shot in the chest and fingers by police and Chhatra League members in front of the Allah Karim Mosque in Mohammadpur, Dhaka.

According to the witness, her daughter Lamia became mentally devastated after the rape occurred and subsequently committed suicide.

The testimony was given in a case against 28 people, including former DSCC Mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Tapos and AL Presidium member Jahangir Kabir Nanak, for crimes against humanity.

Ruma described the harrowing experience of trying to recover her husband's body from hospitals and police stations, claiming she was told by a police officer that clearance was denied due to 'orders from above'.

She further alleged that the police in Dumki, Patuakhali, ordered her to quickly bury the husband's body immediately upon arrival at their village home.

headline: Court writ Writ seeks suspension of Awami League activities ban in High Court
summary: A legal challenge has been filed in the petition to lift the ban on the activities of the Awami League party.
details: A writ petition has been filed in the High Court seeking the suspension of the ban on Awami League activities.
The petition argues that the ban prevents the party from operating legally and restricts its political participation.
The petition seeks a legal review of the the ban's validity and asks the court to allow the party to operate again.
This development comes amidst ongoing political tensions and changes in the interim government's approach to political parties.
The court is set to review the petition writ as part of the legal process to determine the a party's right to political activity.
caption:
Can the Awami League return to political activity? A new court writ seeks to lift the ban.

A writ petition has been filed in the High Court seeking the suspension of the ban on Awami League activities.

The petition argues that the ban prevents the party from operating legally and restricts its political participation.

The petition seeks a legal review of the the ban's validity and asks the court to allow the party to operate again.

This development comes amidst ongoing political tensions and changes in the interim government's approach to political parties.

The court is set to review the petition writ as part of the legal process to determine the a party's right to political activity.
